items.title: Meadowlark Winter Walk of Lights near DC: kids 2 to 12 free on six nights
items.when: November 11, 2026 to January 3, 2027 at Meadowlark Botanical Gardens, Vienna, Virginia. Open 5:30 to 10 p.m. through December 3, then 5 to 10 p.m.; last entry 9:30 p.m. Kids Nights: November 11, 16, 23 and 30, December 14 and January 2. The promotions page gives no year; we read these as this season. Only January 2 falls on a weekend.
items.cost: Per ticket, before tax and fees: $19 online or $24 at the door (November 11 to December 3 and January 1 to 3); $23, online only, December 4 to 31. No separate child price is listed. On Kids Nights, one free ticket for a child 2 to 12 with each paying guest. Parking is free. Two adults and two kids 2 to 12 on a Kids Night: $38, or $46 on December 14, against $76 or $92 if all four paid the listed price (estimate, before tax and fees).
items.booking: Online tickets are for a set entry time, and entry closes 30 minutes after it. For Kids Nights, add the "Kids Night BOGO Ticket, ages 2-12" when you buy online; it can't be combined with other discounts, and tickets already bought are not refunded. Tickets are non-refundable; you can rebook online before 2 p.m. on your date. It runs rain, snow or shine.
items.family: NOVA Parks recommends strollers: the one-way trail is paved and ADA accessible, about half a mile (NOVA Parks also says 0.6 mile), and it suggests 30 to 90 minutes. Hot drinks, pretzels and make-your-own s'mores are on site; no outside food. Parking is limited, so NOVA Parks suggests carpooling. The pages do not say whether children under 2 need a ticket.
items.source_label: NOVA Parks Winter Walk of Lights pages (tickets, promotions, rules)

post.when: Nov 11, 16, 23, 30, Dec 14 and Jan 2, in Vienna, VA. Only Jan 2 is a weekend.
post.cost: $38 for 2 adults + 2 kids, not $76: save about $38 (est.). Dec 14: $46, not $92. Before tax and fees.
post.catch: One free kid per paying guest, added online. No refunds.
post.top_cost: Kids Nights: $38 for 2 adults + 2 kids 2 to 12, $46 on Dec 14 (est., before tax and fees).

items.title: Chicago's Magnificent Mile Lights Festival: free parade and fireworks
items.when: Saturday, November 21, 2026. Booths with free Santa photos 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. at 401 N. Michigan Avenue; parade 5:30 p.m. from Oak Street, heading south along Michigan Avenue; fireworks near the DuSable Bridge at about 7:15 to 7:30 p.m. (official pages differ).
items.cost: Free: Choose Chicago, the city tourism board, lists the festival cost as free. Santa photos at the booths are free. Getting there can cost: the organizer lists a Metra (commuter rail) Saturday Day Pass at $7 per adult, with up to three children 11 and under free per paying adult, and paid garage parking.
items.booking: No tickets are listed for watching from the street; ticketed seating is not mentioned. Streets start closing as early as 8 a.m.; Michigan Avenue closes from Oak to Wacker from 3 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. The DuSable Bridge closes to walkers as early as 3 p.m.; the Columbus Drive Bridge is the organizer's alternative.
items.family: The organizer says the east side of Michigan Avenue is less crowded, especially at the north end, and that Wacker Drive is a good fireworks spot. Our planning note: fireworks run late for small kids, so Santa by day or the parade alone may suit them better. Stroller rules are not stated. It also streams live on abc7chicago.com.

post.when: Sat Nov 21, Michigan Avenue: parade 5:30 p.m., fireworks after 7 p.m.
post.cost: Free. Metra optional: $7 an adult, kids 11 and under free (family of 4 $14 est.).
post.catch: Free Santa photos 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. DuSable Bridge can close to walkers from 3 p.m.

items.booking: No booking listed. The museum's visitor guide says it can be crowded and loud, and people take turns at the display.
items.family: Strollers are not allowed in the gallery, and unattended strollers are not allowed anywhere in the terminal, so the museum suggests leaving yours at home. Per its visitor guide (no year shown), model trains are in a large case, kids can't touch, and you can ask for a scavenger hunt sheet. The museum says the Main Concourse is wheelchair accessible from Lexington Avenue and 42nd Street, not Vanderbilt; it doesn't describe the route to the gallery.

items.title: JetBlue holiday checked bags: $49 and $69 on peak dates
items.when: Peak bag prices apply November 19 to 30, December 17 to 31 and January 1 to 18. November 5 to 18 and December 1 to 16 are off-peak.
items.cost: Per bag, Main and EvenMore fares, U.S., Caribbean, Latin America and Canada routes. Peak dates: $49 first bag, $69 second, when added at least 24 hours before departure. JetBlue says those prices include $10 savings, so at least $59 and $79 later, by our arithmetic; this page lists no airport price. Off-peak: $45 and $59, including $4 and $10 savings. Family of 4 estimate on peak dates, 2 checked bags there and back: $196, or at least $236 if added later. It assumes 2 travelers check one bag each and pay each way; JetBlue's pages list prices per bag and do not state per traveler or each way. One person checking both bags pays the $69 second-bag price: $236 there and back at the lower price.
items.booking: Add bags before check-in, at least 24 hours before departure, for the lower price. JetBlue lists the first bag as included for JetBlue Plus and Premier cardmembers, with conditions in its footnotes. A third or later bag is $200.
items.family: JetBlue's contract says one infant stroller and one infant car seat can be checked at no charge, on top of your bags. JetBlue says strollers are not covered for damage if checked. Lap infants get no checked bag allowance, and playpens count as a bag. These prices apply across the routes listed, not only from New York; other airlines differ.

post.when: Peak prices Nov 19 to 30, Dec 17 to 31, Jan 1 to 18. U.S., Caribbean, Latin America, Canada routes.
post.cost: Main and EvenMore: $49 first bag, $69 second, 24+ hours ahead; at least $10 more a bag later.
post.catch: Family of 4, 2 people check 1 bag each, there and back: $196, at least $236 if added late (est.)

items.title: Bryant Park Cozy Igloos are back: 90-minute heated sessions
items.when: Open since Thursday, November 5, 2026, by the skating pavilion in the southeast corner of the Rink deck, Bryant Park, Midtown Manhattan. Each session is 90 minutes. Bryant Park's page lists no closing date and no hours.
items.cost: Packages start at $259.61, taxes and fees included (the same page's FAQ says $253.96); the page doesn't say which party size or date that price is for. There are packages for 1-4 and for 5-8 guests, so a family of 4 books the 1-4 package; prices vary by party size and on holiday dates. Each package includes shared drinks and one set food item per guest. Gratuity isn't mentioned. Skating is not included.
items.booking: Book a package online through the page's Peek link; you can't sit in an igloo without one. No refunds; you can reschedule up to 48 hours before by email or phone. Bring the card you paid with and the buyer's ID.
items.family: All ages welcome; kids under 2 don't need a food item but count toward the 8-person limit. Heated and open rain, snow or shine, but Bryant Park may cancel for severe weather (the page doesn't say what happens to your booking then); an extra layer helps below freezing. You can't move between the rink and the igloo during a session. Strollers aren't covered on the page. No outside food.

post.when: Open now at Bryant Park, Midtown. 90 minutes; all ages.
post.cost: From $259.61 a package, taxes and fees in (party size not stated); drinks and food included.
post.catch: No refunds; skating not included; holiday prices may differ.

items.title: Wurstfest in New Braunfels: German food, polka and carnival rides, kids 12 and under free
items.when: Friday, November 6 to Sunday, November 15, 2026, at Landa Park in New Braunfels, northeast of San Antonio. Saturdays 11 a.m. to midnight, Sundays 11 a.m. to 10 p.m., weekdays 5 p.m. to 10 or 11 p.m. (opening Friday from 4 p.m.).
items.cost: Kids 12 and under free every day. Adults, online: $15 Fridays and Sundays, $25 Saturdays; at the gate $20 and $30. Monday to Thursday free for everyone, and the last Sunday is free after 3 p.m. Estimate for 2 adults and 2 kids 12 or under: $0 Monday to Thursday, $30 on a Friday or Sunday, $50 on a Saturday, online. Park 'N Ride: free parking, shuttle $10 per person 13 and up, so $20 for 2 adults (per-ride or round trip not stated); no fees listed; ride and carnival prices not listed.
items.booking: Buy online ahead: it is $5 cheaper per adult than the gate. For ID checks, only physical state-issued IDs are accepted (no digital IDs). Parking next to the grounds is limited; the Park 'N Ride runs from Comal County Fairgrounds, 701 Common Street.
items.family: The festival lists carnival rides and children's groups (Edelweiss Kinder Chor, Kinder Tanzer) among its shows; no kids' area is named. It runs rain or shine, bags are searched, no pets except service animals, no bag chairs. No stroller notes posted. Beer is sold on the grounds.
